    “It’s the economy, stupid.” That 1992 catchphrase by Bill Clinton advisor James Carville is being repeated in the aftermath of the Republican debacle last week. And it’s true that the economy can never be ignored. But “it’s the culture, stupid,” is a more apt refrain.

    People, especially the young, voted nearly 10 socialists into the U.S. Congress, and socialists will now lead four of our largest and most important cities: Fresh York, Los Angeles, Seattle, and our capital.

    How did that happen in the Land of the Free, a country that used to have an in-built immunity to Marxism? Students for two or more generations have been acculturated to believe that Marxism is good and America is bad.

    Professors at these universities had to work assiduously. Americans’ resistance to Marxism used to be so strong that, according to urban legend, Soviet tyrant Josef Stalin was the first to coin the term “American exceptionalism” as he decried American imperviousness to the siren song of communism.

    Industry observers note that in June 1929, Jay Lovestone, leader of the Communist Party USA, visited Moscow to meet Stalin, and told him that the American worker was not interested in revolution. America’s lack of a feudal past, as well as other national character traits, made Americans inherently resistant. Stalin shot back that he was tired of this “heresy of American exceptionalism.”.

    >>> No, Mamdani, Socialism Does Not Increase Affordability.

    That account, coming from Stalin’s biographers and popularized by the Atlantic, has been disputed, and Alexis de Tocqueville had already described the United States as “exceptional” in Democracy in America in 1835. But the story illustrates an notable point. America is exceptional in many important ways—like its unique adherence to Natural Right—but no longer when it comes to being immune to socialism.

    Voters last week elected six upcoming members of the Democratic Socialists of America to the House of Representatives: Reps.-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier (D-NY); Claire Valdez (D-NY); Melat Kiros (D-CO); Donavan McKinney (D-MI); Chris Rabb (D-PA); and Angela Gonzales-Torres (D-CA).

    According to recent reports, this freshman class joins Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) and Rashida Tlaib (D-MI), both first elected in 2018, and Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT), who describes himself as a democratic socialist but is technically an independent.

    And of course, there is the newly introduced Mayor of Washington, D.C., Janeese Lewis George, who won 84% of the vote on Election Day, and Nithya Raman, the new mayor of Los Angeles, both proud socialists.

    According to recent reports, the economy was the No. 1 reason voters gave for voting the way they did. Four in 10 voters named the economy, and 90% mentioned the cost of living was a crucial factor, according to The World Data.

    Color me skeptical. I agree more with economist Steve Moore, who said on Fox News last Friday, after a stellar jobs report that beat expectations by a factor of 10,.

    Sources indicate that I wish that would have come out a week ago, I mean, it could have changed things a lot. And by the way, I wrote a column the day after the election saying it wasn’t about ‘the economy, stupid,’ because the economy is pretty damn strong. I mean, you see it, everything that you all have been saying about what’s going on with construction, with manufacturing, with low unemployment rate, the fact there are more jobs than workers.

    It has been revealed that indeed, GDP is growing at an annualized rate of 3.4% in the last quarter. Private domestic demand is even stronger, rising almost 5%, the fastest in five years. The unemployment rate sits at 4.1%, and layoffs remain low.

    According to recent reports, so, why are the voters so upset? It is true that young white males (a key Trump constituency in 2024) are having a tougher time, with the economy churning out more jobs that are geared to women, and because of discrimination against them due to diversity, equity, and inclusion targets, which continue despite Trump’s best efforts. These voters are facing real pressure points: housing, student debt, gas, groceries, etc.

    In a recent development, the Democrats were also disciplined in their messaging and had a great media ground game. The activist Van Jones explained on CNN that Democratic operatives had a coordinated social media campaign that involved tens of thousands of people acting through the “American Accountability Network,” a lefty consortium of content creators.

    >>> The Surprising New Guardians Of Liberty And What It Means For The Left.

    “The Republicans never figured out what we were doing,” said Jones, who, according to the writer Eitan Fischberger, claimed that this campaign generated 32.5 million daily hits on Instagram, 88.8 million on X and 185 million on Facebook, “driving the kitchen table affordability message and tying that to Democrats on a positive and Republicans on a negative.”.

    That voters then chose candidates with a socialist economic agenda that won’t address existing problems and has failed everywhere it’s been tried lies squarely on the capture by Marxists of the cultural institutions. Why do 60% of Democrats have a favorable view of socialism? They have been indoctrinated by the universities, the schools, the museums, the media, etc.

    Just ask conductor Andris Nelsons, who the Boston Symphony Orchestra fired as part of its ill-advised search for “relevance.” Nelsons brought increased ticket sales, but he was not aligned with the more “inclusive” direction the BSO is misguidedly taking.

    As Heather Mac Donald wrote on City Journal, “The main point of contention between the board and Nelsons … seems to have been the conductor’s allegedly inadequate enthusiasm for the race- and gender-based programming and hiring that became so dominant in the classical music world after the George Floyd riots.”.

    Any conservative who ignores all this, takes Carville to heart, looks at the election results and concludes that all the attention must be trained on the economy, to the exclusion of the oft-derided “culture wars,” will be making a big mistake.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, in a last-ditch attempt to avoid Supreme Court scrutiny of its semiautomatic rifle ban, Cook County has suggested that because the last individual Petitioner in the case against it, Christopher Khaya, said in his deposition years ago that he wants to possess a banned Galil rifle, no Petitioner wants to possess a firearm encompassed within the question presented. (Viramontes is now known as Khaya v. Cook County.)  That argument is unpersuasive. The question presented covers "AR-15 platform and similar semiautomatic rifles," not the AR-15 alone. A Galil rifle is a semiautomatic version of the AK-47 which Cook County bans. As shown in the excerpts below, several of the amicus briefs filed in support of petitioners establish that if any rifle is "similar" to the AR-15, the Galil and other AK-types are.

    Recent findings suggest that "The question presented asks whether the Constitution protects possession of 'AR-15 platform and similar semiautomatic rifles.'" That framing is vital because 'AR-15' does not describe a single firearm." Palmetto State Armory Br. 6.

    "The list of similarly styled rifles that are commonly classified as 'assault weapons' is extensive and would include, for example: AK-47 designs, FN FALs, M1 carbines, M1As, HK 91/93/94s and CETME/PTR clones, SKSs, Kel-Tec rifles, Thompsons, Ruger Mini-14/Mini-30s, FN SCARs, and Steyr AUGs and other bullpup designs. These rifles are likewise banned under most 'assault weapons' laws, including the laws at glitch here. It is therefore essential to measure their popularity as well—not just that of the AR-15, which is but one instance of the banned firearm type." English Br. 13.

    It has been revealed that "Thus, in Smith & Wesson Brands, Inc. v. Estados Unidos Mexicanos, 605 U.S. 280 (2025), this Court unanimously explained that so-called 'military style' assault weapons, … includ[ing] AR-15 rifles, AK-47 rifles, and .50 caliber sniper rifles,' are 'both widely legal and bought by many ordinary consumers,' and '[t]he AR-15 is the most popular rifle in the country.' Id. at 297." GOA Br. 19.

    In a recent development, "A Memphis man used a semiautomatic rifle to shoot two armed robbers who were 'ransack[ing]' his house. Action News 5, Homeowner shoots, kills 2 burglars with AK-47 (June 1, 2018), https://perma.cc/J47A-PFUV." Tennessee Br. 14.

    "AR-15s and similar rifles have different characteristics that appeal to different customers, but all are semiautomatic rifles at heart." Eleven State-Based Firearms Advocacy Organizations Br. 16.

    "Semiautomatic operation fires one round for each trigger activation and uses the energy of firing to chamber the next round. That basic mechanism has been commercially available for generations." Rocky Mountain Gun Owners Br. 9.

    My comment: Obviously, whether it is an AK-47 or AR-15, a semiautomatic action uses gas from firing a round to do the "autoloading function," so if semiautomatic rifles are to be protected under the Second Amendment, it should not matter whether the Court rules in a case involving an AR-15 semiautomatic rifle or an AK-47 style semiautomatic rifle.

    Brief of Commonwealth Second Amendment at 8–9.

    Brief of American Firearms Association at 3–4.

    The Three Values That Are the Real Keys to America’s Greatness

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2814 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Heritage

    ⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The midterm postmortem will continue for some time.
    • The midterm postmortem will continue for some time.
    • But as The Daily Wire hosts noted, there is an even deeper problem that needs attention: no one has made a “robust argument for Americanism as an argument, a fully fleshed out argument.” What are the values that make America, America?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The midterm postmortem will continue for some time. Conservatives need careful data analysis from people who can interpret the numbers and understand politics, and politicians who can respond to public opinion with prudence and guiding rhetoric.But as The Daily Wire hosts noted, there is an even deeper problem that needs attention: no one has made a “robust argument for Americanism as an argument, a fully fleshed out argument.” What are the values that make America, America? What is the positive vision?America as a nation is defined by the organic intertwining of people, place, and principles. Each contributes something unique, and they reinforce one another to form a whole even greater than the sum of its parts.James Madison’s theory of separation of powers and checks and balances provides a helpful analogy. Each branch of government has particular responsibilities, but they are not strictly divided from one another. Instead, each branch holds pieces of the others. The president, for example, has the power to veto legislation, giving the executive branch a legislative function. With this dynamic, the three branches check each other to ensure that all act with fidelity and cohere as a single entity.>>> How To Win Back the Disillusioned American DreamThe same is true of the American nation of people, place, and principles.PeopleAmerica is a people sustained over generations by what Americans hold in common: language, history, traditions, and religion, to name a few. As John Jay wrote in Federalist 2:Providence has been pleased to give this one connected country to one united people—a people descended from the same ancestors, speaking the same language, professing the same religion, attached to the same principles of government, very similar in their manners and customs, and who, by their joint counsels, arms, and efforts, fighting side by side throughout a long and bloody war, have nobly established general liberty and independence.A shared culture binds Americans together and supports American principles. For example, speaking the same language allows neighbors to interact, thereby building goodwill and friendship. Communication also enables civic participation and deliberation, which are necessary for self-government.Religious institutions have historically played a major role in that deliberation. Churches are gathering places and seedbeds for community activity; they are the most vital civic associations. At the time of the Founding, 70–80% of American colonists attended services regularly, and the ideas of the Revolution, consistent with biblical principles, spread through sermons, pamphlets, and newspapers.Religion is not the only way a people sustain itself. As George Washington wrote in his Farewell Address, an individual can develop a moral framework independently, but “reason and experience both forbid us to expect that National morality can prevail in exclusion of religious principle.” The Founders and ancient philosophers alike argued that a republic cannot survive without a virtuous people, and religious belief and practice are indispensable for morality.PlaceHuman embodiment comes with an instinctive love of home. America’s physical wonders and gifts inspire awe and gratitude. A sense of reverence reigns over the places where many of our ancestors gave the last full measure of their devotion. And fondness builds in the communities where Americans practice civic rituals and raise posterity. These attachments are good and serious.Yet America as a place is even more: it has fostered American principles and formed the national character.From the outset, James Madison argued that America’s extended territory mitigates the problem of faction: groups adverse to the common good. America has numerous factions, which makes it harder for any single faction to gain a majority. Instead, people and representatives must work with one another and communicate to achieve their goals. That deliberative process slows things down and makes it more likely that justice will prevail.John Jay further observed that America was composed not of “detached and distant territories” but of “one connected, fertile, wide-spreading country” with a “succession of navigable waters” almost made “to bind it together.” The Founders’ response to America as a place was consistent with democratic principles and reinforced the sovereignty of the people.Through the Potomac River Project, which connected regions by roads and waterways, George Washington sought to bind the nation and the character of the American people. Thomas Jefferson led the repeal of primogeniture and entail laws in Virginia. The Northwest Ordinance of 1787 extended that vision to the frontier, and the taming of America’s heartland was given over to those who would steward the land, rather than left to be worked by the many and owned by a few aristocrats.The frontier spirit is part of the American heritage as a result. Americans are adventurous, informal, resilient, industrious, and somewhat gritty. Both the yeoman farmer and the entrepreneur animate the American moral imagination, as America’s physical resources, free institutions, and the human capacity for creativity unleashed profound prosperity.PrinciplesAmerica is the experiment in self-government, and self-government has a multi-layered meaning.Self-government at the institutional level means republican government, in which the people have a real say in the nation’s laws through mechanisms such as popular elections. As James Madison wrote, “no other form” of government “would be reconcilable with the genius of the people of America; with the fundamental principles of the Revolution; or with that honorable determination which animates every votary of freedom, to rest all our political experiments on the capacity of mankind for self-government.”As Madison suggests, self-government at the individual level underlies republican government. Because human beings have reason and conscience, they are responsible for their actions and can order reason above their passions and impulses.The maxim “all men are created equal” expressed in the Declaration of Independence recognizes the nature of human beings and situates mankind in an ordered universe. As John Adams wrote:[Equality] really means little more than that We are all of the same Species: made by the same God: possessed of Minds and Bodies alike in Essence: having all the same Reason, Passions, Affections and appetites. All Men are Men and not Beasts…. The blind are Men, and not Insects, the deaf are Men and not reptiles, the dumb are Men and not Trees. All these are Men and not Angells…America as a nation is dedicated to these principles, which define the American national character.As distinguished Washington and Founding scholar Dr. William B. Allen has written, Lincoln and others believed that regimes are guided by “a shared view of justice that makes a people a people.     The midterm postmortem will continue for some time. Conservatives need careful data analysis from people who can interpret the numbers and understand politics, and politicians who can respond to public opinion with prudence and guiding rhetoric.

    But as The Daily Wire hosts noted, there is an even deeper problem that needs attention: no one has made a “robust argument for Americanism as an argument, a fully fleshed out argument.” What are the values that make America, America? What is the positive vision?

    America as a nation is defined by the organic intertwining of people, place, and principles. Each contributes something unique, and they reinforce one another to form a whole even greater than the sum of its parts.

    Recent findings suggest that james Madison’s theory of separation of powers and checks and balances provides a helpful analogy. Each branch of government has particular responsibilities, but they are not strictly divided from one another. Instead, each branch holds pieces of the others. The president, for example, has the power to veto legislation, giving the executive branch a legislative function. With this dynamic, the three branches check each other to ensure that all act with fidelity and cohere as a single entity.

    >>> How To Win Back the Disillusioned American Dream.

    The same is true of the American nation of people, place, and principles.

    People.

    Recent findings suggest that america is a people sustained over generations by what Americans hold in common: language, history, traditions, and religion, to name a few. As John Jay wrote in Federalist 2:.

    Providence has been pleased to give this one connected country to one united people—a people descended from the same ancestors, speaking the same language, professing the same religion, attached to the same principles of government, very similar in their manners and customs, and who, by their joint counsels, arms, and efforts, fighting side by side throughout a long and bloody war, have nobly established general liberty and independence.

    A shared culture binds Americans together and supports American principles. For example, speaking the same language allows neighbors to interact, thereby building goodwill and friendship. Communication also enables civic participation and deliberation, which are necessary for self-government.

    Religious institutions have historically played a major role in that deliberation. Churches are gathering places and seedbeds for community activity; they are the most key civic associations. At the time of the Founding, 70–80% of American colonists attended services regularly, and the ideas of the Revolution, consistent with biblical principles, spread through sermons, pamphlets, and newspapers.

    According to recent reports, religion is not the only way a people sustain itself. As George Washington wrote in his Farewell Address, an individual can develop a moral framework independently, but “reason and experience both forbid us to expect that National morality can prevail in exclusion of religious principle.” The Founders and ancient philosophers alike argued that a republic cannot survive without a virtuous people, and religious belief and practice are indispensable for morality.

    Place.

    In a recent development, human embodiment comes with an instinctive love of home. America’s physical wonders and gifts inspire awe and gratitude. A sense of reverence reigns over the places where many of our ancestors gave the last full measure of their devotion. And fondness builds in the communities where Americans practice civic rituals and raise posterity. These attachments are good and serious.

    Yet America as a place is even more: it has fostered American principles and formed the national character.

    It has been revealed that from the outset, James Madison argued that America’s extended territory mitigates the problem of faction: groups adverse to the common good. America has numerous factions, which makes it harder for any single faction to gain a majority. Instead, people and representatives must work with one another and communicate to achieve their goals. That deliberative process slows things down and makes it more likely that justice will prevail.

    John Jay further observed that America was composed not of “detached and distant territories” but of “one connected, fertile, wide-spreading country” with a “succession of navigable waters” almost made “to bind it together.” The Founders’ response to America as a place was consistent with democratic principles and reinforced the sovereignty of the people.

    Through the Potomac River Project, which connected regions by roads and waterways, George Washington sought to bind the nation and the character of the American people. Thomas Jefferson led the repeal of primogeniture and entail laws in Virginia. The Northwest Ordinance of 1787 extended that vision to the frontier, and the taming of America’s heartland was given over to those who would steward the land, rather than left to be worked by the many and owned by a few aristocrats.

    The frontier spirit is part of the American heritage as a result. Americans are adventurous, informal, resilient, industrious, and somewhat gritty. Both the yeoman farmer and the entrepreneur animate the American moral imagination, as America’s physical resources, free institutions, and the human capacity for creativity unleashed profound prosperity.

    Principles.

    America is the experiment in self-government, and self-government has a multi-layered meaning.

    Self-government at the institutional level means republican government, in which the people have a real say in the nation’s laws through mechanisms such as popular elections. As James Madison wrote, “no other form” of government “would be reconcilable with the genius of the people of America; with the fundamental principles of the Revolution; or with that honorable determination which animates every votary of freedom, to rest all our political experiments on the capacity of mankind for self-government.”.

    It has been revealed that as Madison suggests, self-government at the individual level underlies republican government. Because human beings have reason and conscience, they are responsible for their actions and can order reason above their passions and impulses.

    The maxim “all men are created equal” expressed in the Declaration of Independence recognizes the nature of human beings and situates mankind in an ordered universe. As John Adams wrote:.

    Sources indicate that [Equality] really means little more than that We are all of the same Species: made by the same God: possessed of Minds and Bodies alike in Essence: having all the same Reason, Passions, Affections and appetites. All Men are Men and not Beasts…. The blind are Men, and not Insects, the deaf are Men and not reptiles, the dumb are Men and not Trees. All these are Men and not Angells….

    America as a nation is dedicated to these principles, which define the American national character.

    Industry observers note that as distinguished Washington and Founding scholar Dr. William B. Allen has written, Lincoln and others believed that regimes are guided by “a shared view of justice that makes a people a people. This was a very old idea, one expressed by Plato, and Aristotle, and Cicero, and Aquinas, and even Jefferson.”.

    Shared understanding imposes limits on behavior and introduces the possibility of friendship, love, and goodwill. As a people, Americans have declared that “life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness” are inalienable rights, and that rights and duties are non-negotiable. Citizens can reasonably take for granted that neighbors will not use force or steal one another’s property, and those boundaries allow interaction and harmony.

    Conclusion.

    Articulating a positive vision of the American nation helps identify policy solutions and cultural difficulties.

    Challenges to self-government include the growth of the administrative state and the erosion of deliberation by instant communication.

    >>> Freedom Isn’t Automatic—Each Generation Must Fight To Keep It.

    This customizable and disembodied world erodes shared memories and experiences. Americans are less likely to gather for small-town parades and fireworks, as spending a solitary evening of Netflix and Uber Eats is more comfortable than eating a hot dog with a neighbor. For such reasons, preserving and defending the physical historic sites that transmit the American story and bring citizens together is even more urgent.

    Political and legal decisions have driven religion out of the public square, and churches have lost parishioners as they have diluted doctrine and required less of the human person.

    It has been revealed that immigration remains a concern as insular communities fail to assimilate into the American way of life. Explaining why others should assimilate requires educating the native-born population in the nation’s Founding principles, so its members can articulate why America is exceptional and worthy of loyalty.

    The nation’s Founding story teaches Americans who they are: a people committed to the principles of self-government, rights and duties, human equality, and the dictates of the natural order.

    These are just a few solutions that would reinforce people, place, and principles. Clarity about what constitutes the American nation guides policy prescriptions. Establishing that clarity is a necessary step in responding to the midterms.

    A Pro-Life Progress Report for the 119th Congress and the Administration

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5539 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Heritage

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • From appropriations to the reconciliation process, the 119th Congress protected taxpayers from supporting abortion and abortion businesses.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Four years ago, the Supreme Court corrected a grave legal error and overturned Roe v. Wade. With abortion no longer enshrined as a “right” in the Constitution, policymakers at all levels of government have stepped up to promote life in law, policy, and culture. For the first session of each latest Congress, The Heritage Foundation provides pro-life policy recommendations to Members and the presidential Administration. The following year, a progress report takes stock of what has been accomplished and what remains on the to-do list. Last year, President Donald Trump and a Republican majority in Congress took the reins. Heritage provided a pro-life policy road map of ways to reverse four years of President Joe Biden’s pro-abortion radicalism.[REF] Now, this Backgrounder analyzes legislative and administrative accomplishments and highlights additional ways the Administration and Congress can protect life.In CongressFrom appropriations to the reconciliation process, the 119th Congress protected taxpayers from supporting abortion and abortion businesses.LegislationCongress advanced important legislation to promote a culture of life.Defunding Substantial Abortion. Congress’s signature pro-life victory in 2025 was the One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB) budget reconciliation measure. It included a provision preventing abortion providers like Planned Parenthood from receiving Medicaid reimbursements for one year.[REF] Medicaid makes up most of Planned Parenthood’s annual federal funding sources. In 2025, more than 50 clinics closed their doors, and across the country Planned Parenthood clinics are feeling the financial strain.[REF] Some blue states have stepped in to try to supplement funding but this is not sustainable in the long run.[REF] Both Planned Parenthood and blue state Attorneys General went to court to try to block the defund provision from taking effect, but were ultimately unsuccessful.[REF] Congress holds the power of the purse, and nothing in the Constitution entitles the abortion industry to Americans’ hard-earned tax dollars. As discussed below under “More to Accomplish,” another reconciliation bill could allow the defunding provision to extend beyond the OBBB’s one-year time frame, which has already passed. Planned Parenthood and other large abortion providers became eligible to receive Medicaid funds again on July 4, 2026.[REF]Supporting Pregnant and Parenting Students. In January 2026, the House of Representatives passed the Pregnant Students’ Rights Act (H.R. 6359),[REF] which requires universities to provide pregnant women and girls with information about their rights, resources, and available accommodations.Pregnancy Resource Center Support. Also in January 2026, the House also passed the Supporting Pregnant and Parenting Women and Families Act (H.R. 6945),[REF] which provides statutory clarity that states can direct Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) funding to pregnancy resource centers that support mothers, families, and unborn children through services like counseling, material support, and education.Addressing Weaponization and Selective Enforcement. The House Judiciary Committee approved the FACE Act Repeal Act (H.R. 589)[REF] in June 2025. The bill is needed in light of intense weaponization by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) under President Biden, which is also discussed below. The Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrances (FACE) Act[REF] was enacted in 1994 and prohibits physically obstructing, injuring, intimidating, or interfering with anyone “obtaining or providing reproductive health services.” Under President Biden, the DOJ deliberately targeted peaceful pro-life Americans while failing to vigorously enforce FACE Act protections that apply to churches and pregnancy centers, which faced increasing attacks following the Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade. Sufficient laws already exist at the state level to address criminal activity, so Congress should repeal the FACE Act once and for all.AppropriationsCongress stood firm to protect life via spending legislation.Maintaining Status Quo of Pro-Life Policies. House-passed appropriations legislation has incorporated numerous pro-life policy riders, such as the Hyde family of amendments that prohibit taxpayer funding for abortions in foreign and domestic programs. However, new pro-life policy riders are routinely stripped during negotiations between the House and Senate.[REF]Addressing Problematic Earmarks. In FY 2024, two hospitals that perform late-term abortion procedures received almost $2.5 million in federal funds via earmarks in that year’s Labor-HHS [U.S. Department of Health and Human Services] funding.[REF] Those were Senate earmarks; the House Labor–HHS subcommittee accepted no earmark requests for FY 2024 through FY 2026.[REF] For FY 2027, the House Appropriations Committee’s Labor–HHS subcommittee provided guidance for earmark requests.[REF] Among requirements going forward, entities that perform or promote abortions are not eligible. Entities that conduct research using embryonic stem cells obtained from an induced abortion, or human germline gene modification, are not eligible. And entities that facilitate sex-rejecting interventions are not eligible.In the Trump AdministrationThe Trump Administration played a significant role in advancing pro-life policies.Previous Executive Orders and PoliciesIn 2025, the Administration rapidly acted on a host of policies, which are discussed in the 2025 Backgrounder.[REF] They include:An executive order to disentangle taxpayers from abortion funding.[REF]Reinstatement of the Protecting Life in Global Health Assistance policy, which disentangles foreign aid dollars from international nongovernmental organizations that perform or promote abortions.[REF] As discussed in the following section, the policy has since been expanded.Defunding of the United Nations Population Fund over its complicity with China’s coercive and inhumane population-control practices.[REF]Renewal of membership in the Geneva Consensus Declaration, a partnership of more than 40 countries committed to improving women’s health, protecting innocent life, and strengthening the family.[REF]Partial restoration of Title X family planning program funding to Oklahoma[REF] and Tennessee.[REF] These pro-life states were denied funding by the Biden Administration over their refusal to provide abortion counseling and referrals.Recission of a Department of Defense abortion travel policy that made travel and transportation allowances available to service members and their dependents for abortions.[REF]Rescission of Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) guidance that wrongly claimed that EMTALA requires doctors to perform elective abortions.[REF]Pro-Life Regulations, Executive Orders, and Other PoliciesOver the past year and a half, the Trump Administration has taken additional steps to promote life-affirming policies. These steps include:Taxpayer Funding for Abortions. In July 2025, the Department of Justice issued an opinion[REF] that the Hyde Amendment, which prohibits taxpayer dollars from paying for elective abortions, means that the HHS cannot spend taxpayer dollars to provide “ancillary services necessary to receive an abortion”—such as the Office of Refugee Resettlement providing transportation for women seeking an abortion. The HHS has said it is reviewing the relevant regulations and guidance.[REF]Abortion in Obamacare Intends. On December 9, 2025, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) issued guidance[REF] about Section 1303 of the Affordable Care Act’s abortion coverage accounting gimmick. Section 1303 requires insurers to collect a separate payment for certain abortion coverage in qualified health plans approved to be sold on the exchanges. Maryland and other pro-abortion states attempted to commandeer excess funds remaining in abortion surcharge accounts to establish grant programs to pay for additional abortion travel and elective abortions.[REF] The CMS clarified that the leftover funds belong to insurers—not states seeking to subsidize additional abortions.As discussed below under “More to Accomplish,” the CMS should re-issue the Section 1303 regulation from President Trump’s first term. In December 2019, the CMS adopted a rule[REF] interpreting that separate payments be just that—separate—and that issuers needed to comply with the letter and spirit of Obamacare requirements. The same has not been true under Presidents Barack Obama and Biden. The CMS should rescind the Biden rule and return to the rule in place during President Trump’s first term.Abortion at the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). On December 18, 2025, the DOJ issued an opinion[REF] that the Biden Administration overstepped its authority by issuing a regulation requiring abortion procedures, referrals, and counseling to veterans at VA medical facilities. The VA quickly issued a memorandum returning to pre-2022 policies that excluded abortion and abortion counseling.[REF] On December 31, the VA issued a final rule formally rescinding the 2022 Biden Administration rule that returned to the pre-2022 abortion exclusions.[REF]International Abortion Funding. In January 2026, the Trump Administration announced that it is further expanding life-affirming foreign aid policies. Since the 1980s the Mexico City Policy has required (under Republican Administrations) foreign nongovernmental organizations to certify that they will not perform or promote abortion as a condition of receiving U.S. family planning assistance. During President Trump’s first Administration, that policy was expanded to apply to more funding streams and called the Protecting Life in Global Health Assistance Policy. Now, under a new name. the Promoting Human Flourishing in Foreign Assistance (PHFFA) Policy has expanded to encompass abortion,[REF] radical gender ideology,[REF] and diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI)[REF] policies as well.Fetal Tissue Research. In January 2026, the National Institutes of Health (NIH) reinstated a policy from President Trump’s first term ending support for unethical and obsolete research using fetal tissue obtained from elective abortion. The prohibition applies to internal and external projects (such as grants to outside entities). [REF] The NIH can prioritize ethical alternatives instead.Planned Parenthood COVID-19 “Relief” Funding. In January 2026, the Small Business Administration (SBA) announced that it is reviewing whether Planned Parenthood affiliates improperly received more than $88 million in loans during the COVID-19 pandemic. The SBA is demanding that Planned Parenthood clinics either prove that they were eligible to receive Paycheck Protection Program loans or return the funding.[REF] During President Trump’s first term, the SBA preliminarily concluded that Planned Parenthood affiliates were not eligible to receive these loans that were meant to help small businesses, but the Biden Administration later forgave many of those loans.[REF]Department of Justice Weaponization. In April 2026, the DOJ issued an extensive report detailing how the DOJ under President Biden weaponized the FACE Act against pro-life Americans.[REF] The report concluded: (1) The DOJ violated Americans’ rights through biased enforcement; (2) the DOJ collaborated with pro-abortion organizations to track pro-life activists’ activity; (3) prosecutors repeatedly engaged in inappropriate conduct; (4) the DOJ sought harsher punishment for pro-life activists than for pro-abortion activists; and (5) the DOJ inappropriately tried to help a pro-abortion organization with an application for a grant.Reviewing Human Embryonic Stem Cell Research. In January 2026, the NIH announced a pause on submissions to the NIH Human Embryonic Stem Cell Registry and issued a request for information on ways to reduce—and potentially replace—current reliance on research using human embryonic stem cells.[REF]Pro-Life Budget Request for FY 2027. In April 2026, the Office of Management and Budget released its budget request for the upcoming fiscal year. The request includes long-standing provisions in current law, such as Hyde protections across multiple departments (foreign and domestic), conscience protections, and bioethics-related funding restrictions for certain research. Additional requests include protections separating foreign aid funding from organizations that perform or promote abortions, including additional conscience protections for medical trainees, stripping Planned Parenthood of any HHS funding, and ending funding for fetal tissue research.[REF] This proposal is a request and Congress will ultimately decide FY 2027 funding and dollar amounts. As with the FY 2026 request, the Administration demonstrated its strong commitment to pro-life policymaking throughout the government.Redirecting Teen Pregnancy Prevention Funding to Align with Pro-Family Priorities. In June 2026, the HHS canceled most federal Teen Pregnancy Prevention Program grants two years early, some of which had gone to comprehensive sex-education curricula taught by abortion providers like Planned Parenthood. The HHS opened new funding opportunities that will be available to grantees who align programming with the Administration’s priorities of sexual risk avoidance education and not encouraging, normalizing, or promoting sexual activity for minors.[REF]Conscience RightsThe Trump Administration is prioritizing enforcement of federal conscience protection laws. The HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR) is ensuring that no person or organization is discriminated against over their convictions on abortion and gender ideology.In January 2026, the OCR announced a list of enforcement actions and policy changes, including:A notice of violation determining that the Illinois law requiring abortion referrals violates the Weldon and Coats–Snowe Amendments.[REF]A nationwide “Dear Colleague” letter summarizing federal health care conscience protections that the OCR is tasked with enforcing and reaffirming the Administration’s commitment to protect individuals and organizations from being discriminated against due to their sincere moral or religious convictions.[REF]Recission of Biden Administration guidance that wrongly claims that federal law on emergency medical care requires doctors to perform elective abortions.[REF]Recission of Biden Administration guidance that wrongly instructed pharmacies to stock and dispense dangerous abortion pills, even though pharmacies and pharmacists have a right to not violate their conscience by participating in abortion. Under President Biden, the HHS walked back part of this guidance after losing a court case to pharmacies challenging the guidance.[REF] Now the guidance has been rescinded entirely.[REF]Disavowal of[REF] the Biden Administration’s August 2021 decision to withdraw the Trump Administration’s 2020 Notice of Violation that California broke federal conscience rights law over its insurance coverage mandate for elective abortion.Disavowal of[REF] the Biden Administration’s July 2021 decision to withdraw the Trump Administration’s Notice of Violation that the University of Vermont Medical Center broke federal conscience rights law by requiring a health care professional to participate in an abortion procedure despite strong objection.In March 2026, the HHS announced that the OCR is investigating 13 states over possible violations of the Weldon Amendment, which states government cannot discriminate against health care entities that do not pay for or provide coverage of abortions.[REF] The states under investigation have abortion coverage requirements for plans sold in their respective jurisdictions.[REF]In May 2026, the HHS announced an additional reorganization within the OCR.[REF] The OCR is tasked with enforcing federal civil rights laws related to conscience, religious freedom, privacy, cybersecurity, and more. In 2018, during President Trump’s first term, the HHS created a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division within the OCR. Under President Biden, this division was shuttered and absorbed, with the Civil Rights Division, into the Policy Division.[REF] Rights of conscience and religious freedom are not “less than.” Restoring the Conscience and Religious Freedom Division will provide the OCR with the tools it needs to best serve all Americans and ensure that their fundamental rights are respected.More to AccomplishBoth Congress and the Administration have successfully advanced important pro-life policies, but there is still more work to do.In CongressDefunding Big Abortion, maintaining long-standing pro-life policy riders, and holding bad actors accountable must continue to be a priority.Planned Parenthood. Preventing Planned Parenthood and other abortion providers from receiving Medicaid reimbursements for one year was a signature accomplishment in the 2025 OBBB budget reconciliation package. Medicaid makes up most of Planned Parenthood’s federal funding sources. However, this defunding provision was the only one in the entire bill subject to a one-year time frame rather than the full 10 years to which the bill can apply. Planned Parenthood and other large abortion providers became eligible to receive Medicaid funds again on July 4, 2026.[REF] If Congress discusses another reconciliation bill, the defunding provision should be incorporated for the full 10-year time frame so that taxpayers do not have to continue funding abortion providers.Appropriations. Congress has continued to include long-standing riders like the Hyde Amendment and similar language in annual appropriations bills, prohibiting taxpayer dollars from paying for most abortions. But many other pro-life policies can be enacted via appropriations riders. From expanding conscience protections to reinstating commonsense safety protections for risky abortion pills, there is more that Congress should do to promote life in must-pass spending legislation.[REF]Oversight. Congress should continue to invoke its oversight and investigatory role to hold bad actors accountable and ensure that that pro-life priorities in the Administration are not sidelined. For example, in 2022, activists obtained the remains of five preemie-size unborn babies who had been aborted at a notorious Washington, DC, late-term abortion mill. According to expert testimony, these babies may have been aborted using the illegal partial-birth abortion technique. One baby was still in the amniotic sac and may have been born alive and left to die.[REF] Local authorities stonewalled questions from Congress and the press about any investigation of this activity. Pro-life activists and Members of Congress feared that the DC Office of the Chief Medical Examiner would destroy the five bodies, but in February 2024 it confirmed that it would not immediately do so.[REF] During a June 2025 hearing, then-Attorney General Pam Bondi indicated that there was an ongoing investigation.[REF]Demand FDA Action on Dangerous Abortion Drugs. Congress should continue demanding transparency from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on its long-promised comprehensive review of the abortion pill. It is abundantly clear that current FDA postmarketing safety policies are not adequately protecting women and children.[REF] In light of the politicized approval process that put this risky drug on the market in the first place, a complete and thorough review is long overdue. Leadership changes at the FDA should not slow down or deprioritize this important work. Individual members and congressional committees should continue emphasizing the dangers these drugs pose to women, girls, and unborn children.In the Trump AdministrationThe Trump Administration should rescind Biden-era regulations and policies that promoted abortion and sought to undermine the 2022 Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade. These include:Abortion Travel for Unaccompanied Illegal Alien Children (UACs). A senior Office of Refugee Resettlement official told The Daily Signal[REF] that the agency is working on reversing a Biden-era regulation allowing taxpayer-funded abortion travel for UACs.[REF] The changes were submitted to the Office of Management and Budget’s Regulatory Information Service Center in January 2026, but the updated regulation has not been formally proposed yet. The HHS should ensure that the rule advances quickly.A Privacy Regulation That Undercut Abuse Reporting. In June 2025, a federal court struck down[REF] most of a Biden Administration regulation that purported to strengthen protections for sensitive private health information, including information related to abortion. In reality, the rule improperly limited state child abuse reporting laws.[REF] The HHS should formally rescind the rule.The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission’s (EEOC) Wrongful Interpretation of the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA). In 2024, the EEOC issued rulemaking interpreting the PWFA’s definition of “medical condition” related to pregnancy to include elective abortion, thus requiring employers to provide accommodations like time off from work to have an abortion or time off to recover from the procedure.[REF] Litigation related to the entire rule is ongoing. In May 2025, a federal court provided nationwide relief for employers who care deeply about the well-being of their employees (and their children, born and unborn) by vacating the elective abortion accommodation provision.[REF] The EEOC should clean up the mess and formally rescind its erroneous interpretation of the PWFA. Pro-life Members of Congress would not have supported this bipartisan bill if it empowered the federal bureaucracy to invent a requirement for abortion accommodations.A Rollback of a Conscience Protection Regulation from President Trump’s First Term. The Biden Administration partially rescinded[REF] President Trump’s 2019 rule about enforcing more than a dozen federal laws that protect conscience rights for individuals or entities that do not want to participate in or facilitate morally fraught procedures such as abortion.[REF] The Biden rule gutted the HHS Office for Civil Rights’ ability to adequately enforce conscience laws that protect Americans’ civil rights. The regulation from President Trump’s first term should be restored.Addressing Title X Family Planning Program Funds Used as a Slush Fund for the Abortion Industry. The Biden Administration rescinded a regulation from President Trump’s first term that required recipients to physically and financially separate all abortion activity from Title X activity and prohibited Title X projects from promoting or referring for abortion.[REF] The Biden regulation also required sites that do not offer a broad range of contraception to provide a prescription or referral. This created a new barrier for sites that offer fertility awareness-based methods (FABMs) but cannot in good conscience provide or refer for other methods. The Title X program should not be used as a slush fund for abortion providers. The Trump Administration should restore the regulation from President Trump’s first term.A Clean Up of Policies Concerning the Affordable Care Act’s (ACA) Nondiscrimination Provision. Among other things, Section 1557 of the ACA prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, disability, and sex in covered health programs or activities.[REF] Just weeks after the Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade, the Biden Administration moved to redefine conditions related to “sex” to include abortion, as the Obama Administration had also done in 2016. The Trump Administration should revive the abortion-related provisions of this regulation from President Trump’s first term, issued in 2020.[REF]Ensuring that Issuers Comply with ACA Abortion Rules. Thirteen states require plans sold on their marketplace to include coverage for abortion. Section 1303 of the ACA says that such plans cannot use federal funds (including premium tax credits and cost-sharing reductions) for elective abortions. Section 1303 also requires issuers to collect a separate payment from each enrollee for the abortion coverage portion and segregate those funds in separate allocation accounts solely used for abortion coverage. Plans are also required to provide notice to enrollees at the time of enrollment that the proposal includes abortion coverage. But under Presidents Obama and Biden, CMS policy was essentially an accounting gimmick that did not enforce the letter or spirit of the ACA. The CMS should re-issue the Section 1303 regulation from President Trump’s first term. That rule[REF] rightly required that separate payments be just that: separate.Stopping Elective Abortions in the Indian Health Service (IHS) Program. The Biden Administration issued a rule that weakens the prohibition on abortion funding within the IHS.[REF] Per the Hyde Amendment, federal funds cannot be used to pay for abortion except in very limited circumstances. Under the Biden rule, if Congress ever fails to include the Hyde Amendment in annual appropriations legislation, then the IHS would be able to fund elective abortions.Robustly Enforcing Federal Conscience Protection Laws. Laws like the Church, Coats–Snowe, and Weldon Amendments are meant to ensure that no one faces discrimination for declining to perform, participate in, or pay for an abortion in HHS-funded programs. Under previous Administrations that prioritized a radical pro-abortion agenda, conscience protection was not a priority. The Trump Administration is reversing that trend. The HHS and the OCR should continue to protect Americans from discrimination in federally funded programs. For example, a February 2026 letter to the HHS from Alliance Defending Freedom identifies 49 HHS-funded family medicine residency programs that, it says, violate federal conscience laws by requiring residents to participate in abortion training.[REF]Prioritizing Health and Safety at the FDA and Department of Justice, Not the Abortion Industry’s Bottom Line. The FDA should expeditiously conduct its long-promised review of the abortion drug mifepristone and revisit the dangerous drug’s approval.     Four years ago, the Supreme Court corrected a grave legal error and overturned Roe v. Wade. With abortion no longer enshrined as a “right” in the Constitution, policymakers at all levels of government have stepped up to promote life in law, policy, and culture. For the first session of each new Congress, The Heritage Foundation provides pro-life policy recommendations to Members and the presidential Administration. The following year, a progress report takes stock of what has been accomplished and what remains on the to-do list. Last year, President Donald Trump and a Republican majority in Congress took the reins. Heritage provided a pro-life policy road map of ways to reverse four years of President Joe Biden’s pro-abortion radicalism.[REF] Now, this Backgrounder analyzes legislative and administrative accomplishments and highlights additional ways the Administration and Congress can protect life.

    From appropriations to the reconciliation process, the 119th Congress protected taxpayers from supporting abortion and abortion businesses.

    Congress advanced vital legislation to promote a culture of life.

    Industry observers note that defunding Big Abortion. Congress’s signature pro-life victory in 2025 was the One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB) budget reconciliation measure. It included a provision preventing abortion providers like Planned Parenthood from receiving Medicaid reimbursements for one year.[REF] Medicaid makes up most of Planned Parenthood’s annual federal funding sources. In 2025, more than 50 clinics closed their doors, and across the country Planned Parenthood clinics are feeling the financial strain.[REF] Some blue states have stepped in to try to supplement funding but this is not sustainable in the long run.[REF] Both Planned Parenthood and blue state Attorneys General went to court to try to block the defund provision from taking effect, but were ultimately unsuccessful.[REF] Congress holds the power of the purse, and nothing in the Constitution entitles the abortion industry to Americans’ hard-earned tax dollars. As discussed below under “More to Accomplish,” another reconciliation bill could allow the defunding provision to extend beyond the OBBB’s one-year time frame, which has already passed. Planned Parenthood and other large abortion providers became eligible to receive Medicaid funds again on July 4, 2026.[REF].

    Supporting Pregnant and Parenting Students. In January 2026, the House of Representatives passed the Pregnant Students’ Rights Act (H.R. 6359),[REF] which requires universities to provide pregnant women and girls with information about their rights, resources, and available accommodations.

    Pregnancy Resource Center Support. Also in January 2026, the House also passed the Supporting Pregnant and Parenting Women and Families Act (H.R. 6945),[REF] which provides statutory clarity that states can direct Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) funding to pregnancy resource centers that support mothers, families, and unborn children through services like counseling, material support, and education.

    Industry observers note that addressing Weaponization and Selective Enforcement. The House Judiciary Committee approved the FACE Act Repeal Act (H.R. 589)[REF] in June 2025. The bill is needed in light of intense weaponization by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) under President Biden, which is also discussed below. The Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrances (FACE) Act[REF] was enacted in 1994 and prohibits physically obstructing, injuring, intimidating, or interfering with anyone “obtaining or providing reproductive health services.” Under President Biden, the DOJ deliberately targeted peaceful pro-life Americans while failing to vigorously enforce FACE Act protections that apply to churches and pregnancy centers, which faced increasing attacks following the Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade. Sufficient laws already exist at the state level to address criminal activity, so Congress should repeal the FACE Act once and for all.

    Congress stood firm to protect life via spending legislation.

    Industry observers note that maintaining Status Quo of Pro-Life Policies. House-passed appropriations legislation has incorporated numerous pro-life policy riders, such as the Hyde family of amendments that prohibit taxpayer funding for abortions in foreign and domestic programs. However, new pro-life policy riders are routinely stripped during negotiations between the House and Senate.[REF].

    According to recent reports, addressing Problematic Earmarks. In FY 2024, two hospitals that perform late-term abortion procedures received almost $2.5 million in federal funds via earmarks in that year’s Labor-HHS [U.S. Department of Health and Human Services] funding.[REF] Those were Senate earmarks; the House Labor–HHS subcommittee accepted no earmark requests for FY 2024 through FY 2026.[REF] For FY 2027, the House Appropriations Committee’s Labor–HHS subcommittee provided guidance for earmark requests.[REF] Among requirements going forward, entities that perform or promote abortions are not eligible. Entities that conduct research using embryonic stem cells obtained from an induced abortion, or human germline gene modification, are not eligible. And entities that facilitate sex-rejecting interventions are not eligible.

    The Trump Administration played a significant role in advancing pro-life policies.

    In January 2026, the OCR announced a list of enforcement actions and policy changes, including:.

    In March 2026, the HHS declared that the OCR is investigating 13 states over possible violations of the Weldon Amendment, which says government cannot discriminate against health care entities that do not pay for or provide coverage of abortions.[REF] The states under investigation have abortion coverage requirements for prepares sold in their respective jurisdictions.[REF].

    In May 2026, the HHS announced an additional reorganization within the OCR.[REF] The OCR is tasked with enforcing federal civil rights laws related to conscience, religious freedom, privacy, cybersecurity, and more. In 2018, during President Trump’s first term, the HHS created a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division within the OCR. Under President Biden, this division was shuttered and absorbed, with the Civil Rights Division, into the Policy Division.[REF] Rights of conscience and religious freedom are not “less than.” Restoring the Conscience and Religious Freedom Division will provide the OCR with the tools it needs to best serve all Americans and ensure that their fundamental rights are respected.

    Both Congress and the Administration have successfully advanced important pro-life policies, but there is still more work to do.

    Defunding Massive Abortion, maintaining long-standing pro-life policy riders, and holding bad actors accountable must continue to be a priority.

    Planned Parenthood. Preventing Planned Parenthood and other abortion providers from receiving Medicaid reimbursements for one year was a signature accomplishment in the 2025 OBBB budget reconciliation package. Medicaid makes up most of Planned Parenthood’s federal funding sources. However, this defunding provision was the only one in the entire bill subject to a one-year time frame rather than the full 10 years to which the bill can apply. Planned Parenthood and other large abortion providers became eligible to receive Medicaid funds again on July 4, 2026.[REF] If Congress discusses another reconciliation bill, the defunding provision should be incorporated for the full 10-year time frame so that taxpayers do not have to continue funding abortion providers.

    Appropriations. Congress has continued to include long-standing riders like the Hyde Amendment and similar language in annual appropriations bills, prohibiting taxpayer dollars from paying for most abortions. But many other pro-life policies can be enacted via appropriations riders. From expanding conscience protections to reinstating commonsense safety protections for risky abortion pills, there is more that Congress should do to promote life in must-pass spending legislation.[REF].

    According to recent reports, oversight. Congress should continue to invoke its oversight and investigatory role to hold bad actors accountable and ensure that that pro-life priorities in the Administration are not sidelined. For example, in 2022, activists obtained the remains of five preemie-size unborn babies who had been aborted at a notorious Washington, DC, late-term abortion mill. According to expert testimony, these babies may have been aborted using the illegal partial-birth abortion technique. One baby was still in the amniotic sac and may have been born alive and left to die.[REF] Local authorities stonewalled questions from Congress and the press about any investigation of this activity. Pro-life activists and Members of Congress feared that the DC Office of the Chief Medical Examiner would destroy the five bodies, but in February 2024 it confirmed that it would not immediately do so.[REF] During a June 2025 hearing, then-Attorney General Pam Bondi indicated that there was an ongoing investigation.[REF].

    Recent findings suggest that demand FDA Action on Dangerous Abortion Drugs. Congress should continue demanding transparency from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on its long-promised comprehensive review of the abortion pill. It is abundantly clear that current FDA postmarketing safety policies are not adequately protecting women and children.[REF] In light of the politicized approval process that put this risky drug on the market in the first place, a complete and thorough review is long overdue. Leadership changes at the FDA should not slow down or deprioritize this important work. Individual members and congressional committees should continue emphasizing the dangers these drugs pose to women, girls, and unborn children.

    The Trump Administration should rescind Biden-era regulations and policies that promoted abortion and sought to undermine the 2022 Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade. These include:.

    According to recent reports, slim Republican–Democrat margins in Congress left little room for error when it comes to any legislative priority, including pro-life policies. That is why tools like budget reconciliation and must-pass appropriations legislation are so critical to advancing protections for babies and mothers.

With the President’s second term in full swing, pro-life Americans expect to see policymakers continue to deliver more meaningful protections for women, girls, and unborn babies.

    Veterans Day is more than a commemoration of military service. It is also a reminder that freedom depends on citizens willing to serve something larger than themselves—and not just when they are in uniform.

    Our service members do much more than most of us realize, and our society is the better for it.

    Across generations, American veterans have answered the nation’s call in war and peace out of a commitment to duty, sacrifice and country. Their example shows that citizenship carries responsibilities as well as rights, and that self-government endures only when citizens place the common good above personal interest.

    The freedoms that Americans enjoy today were secured by all veterans who served. They defended not merely our borders but also the principles upon which this nation was founded: liberty, representative government and the rule of law.

    By defending the constitutional order, veterans helped preserve a nation in which political differences are settled through lawful debate and elections rather than force. Veterans Day is an opportunity to recognize the men and women whose sacrifices have made that peaceful self-government possible.

    >>> The Three Values That Are the Real Keys to America’s Greatness.

    Veterans have helped secure liberty against some of the most oppressive ideologies in human history, including communism and national socialism. American veterans were instrumental in defeating the Nazi regime during World War II, helping liberate Europe from a government built on tyranny, aggression and the systematic denial of human freedom.

    Industry observers note that during the Cold War, generations of American servicemen and women stood watch against the expansion of Soviet communism, preserving the security of the free world through deterrence and steadfast resolve. Their service helped create the conditions that led to the collapse of the Soviet Union and the liberation of millions of people in Central and Eastern Europe.

    The freedom enjoyed today by nations once trapped behind the Iron Curtain is part of the legacy of those veterans who answered their country’s call.

    According to recent reports, across these conflicts, American veterans served as guardians of the principle that free people have the right to govern themselves. Veterans Day also reminds us that liberty is never self-executing. The constitutional freedoms secured through military sacrifice endure only when citizens practice the discipline, responsibility and respect for law that self-government requires.

    The veteran’s example therefore reaches beyond the battlefield, offering a model for preserving freedom in civic life.

    Veterans also participate in freedom’s defense at home at some of the highest rates in American society. According to the 2025 Veterans Civic Health Index, 81% of veterans were registered to vote in the 2024 election, compared with 74% of nonveterans. Seventy-three percent of veterans cast ballots, compared with 66% of nonveterans.

    According to recent reports, the index also reports stronger veteran participation in volunteering, in civic organizations and in engagement with public officials and community institutions. Together, these measures point to a broader pattern: For many veterans, military service becomes a lifelong commitment to citizenship, civic responsibility and the preservation of our constitutional republic.

    According to recent reports, veterans continue to serve as teachers, business leaders, first responders, elected officials and civic volunteers, bringing military habits of integrity, discipline and teamwork into civilian life. At Military.com, Medal of Honor recipient Clint Romesha captures that enduring impulse, saying, “So many of us veterans just want to continue to serve after service.”.

    Sources indicate that mr. Romesha identifies teamwork as one of the military’s greatest lessons—“It’s not about me; it’s about the team”—and as a principle that continues to guide veterans long after they leave the uniform behind.

    Sources indicate that the veteran profiles of “American Heroes: Stories of Service” and “Pledge to Patriots” show this continuing commitment in action. These stories feature veterans mentoring young people, supporting one another, leading nonprofits, responding to disasters and strengthening communities.

    >>> Nina and the Bikers.

    Thousands of veterans serve as poll workers, election officials and observers, helping to administer and safeguard elections. As a former election official and U.S. Navy veteran, I have seen them step forward when communities need poll workers. Through the nonpartisan Vet the Vote initiative, more than 163,000 veterans and military family members served as poll workers during the 2024 election cycle, up from approximately 63,500 during the 2022 midterms.

    In a recent development, national Guard members have supported election operations, security, coordination and emergency response at the request of state authorities. Their commitment to duty, adherence to procedures and record of public service can strengthen confidence in the electoral process they defended in uniform.

    Industry observers note that on Veterans Day, we honor those who wore the uniform in defense of our nation. We should also follow the example they continue to set—as citizens, poll workers, community leaders and public servants—reminding us that freedoms secured on far-off battlefields must be preserved through faithful participation in self-government at home.

    Veterans Day recognizes a profound commitment to country, but it also challenges every American to accept the duties of citizenship.

    It has been revealed that in 2023, I spent four weeks visiting eight of the countries involved in the transit routes to learn why they had come back to life.     “Taliban good!” he told me in pidgin English when I asked his opinion about the ruling terrorist group in his home country.

    A Breach in the Defenses.

    The Balkan routes generally run northwest from Turkey through countries like Greece, Macedonia, Serbia, Bosnia, and Croatia. Migrants know that once they penetrate into the periphery of the E.U., a borderless inter-nation agreement (the Schengen Zone) enables inspection-free travel to rich and desirable interior countries like France.

Because of this mayhem, the E.U.’s external countries buttoned up their borders with stout fences and instant-expulsion policies backed by rigorous patrolling.

When migrants diverted west to avoid it, Austria built another, forcing Slovenia to build a razor-wire fence along the border with Croatia to head off further spillover.

    By 2016, the Balkan routes were considered effectively closed. It also helped that the E.U. paid Turkey and some proxy North African nations (and violent militias) billions of euros to stop and block emigration from their territories.

    So how did another mass migration start in 2022 that would flood France with tens of thousands more?

    In June 2022, Slovenian voters threw out the center-right Slovenian Democratic Party that had built that fence. They elected the center-left Freedom Movement and installed Prime Minister Robert Golob, who had campaigned to tear down Slovenia’s fence and immediately set about doing so.

    Word spread that a gap in Slovenia’s Balkan route had just opened, so migrants came pouring through it. I toured the forlorn remnants of Slovenia’s fence, observing broken-down sections lying where they had been pushed down. Anyone could walk through at will. I never saw a single police officer as I crossed back and forth repeatedly on foot and by car.

    “No problem!!!” almost everyone shouted, laughing as they turned and disappeared into the dark forest, chanting, “Inshallah! Inshallah!”—if God wills it.

    In a recent development, the median American read only two books in 2025, and 40% of us read not a single book all year. The French are more literary; they read an average of 18 books a year. They venerate authors—the more intellectual, controversial, and impenetrable the better.But that doesn’t mean authors are beyond criticism in France. The work of Michel Houellebecq, for example, has long been controversial. In 2002, he was charged with inciting racism for calling Islam “the stupidest religion.” Mosques in Paris and Lyon joined with the World Islamic League to bring the charges against him. Paris judges found him not guilty.In response, the head of the Mosque of Lyon noted, “Islam now can be insulted freely. The permission to insult Islam has now been given.”Well, yes. That’s how free speech works. Insulting a person, institution, or religion may be unfair, unkind, or even unwise, but in these United States at least, it is not illegal. That’s why we tolerate the views of podcast harpy Jennifer Welch and chief “Groyper” Nick Fuentes, among others.But France, like Britain and Germany, has no First Amendment. In all three countries, people are routinely arrested for speech that in the United States would be legal.>>> France’s Education Collapse Is a Warning for AmericaHouellebecq’s book “Submission” was published in January 2015, on the same day Islamist terrorists murdered 12 journalists and staff at the satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo for having republished cartoons depicting the Muslim prophet Mohammed.“Submission” invokes an imaginary future (2022!) where a Muslim party has won national elections and governs according to Sharia law—among other things, legalizing polygamy. The protagonist, a middle-aged man, eventually decides to convert to Islam so he can have more wives.Houellebecq took a lot of criticism for the book but was not formally charged. He was raised as a young child in Algeria at the end of its French rule, which ended in a bloody terrorist campaign and war. That experience may have shaped his bleak view of France’s future.Houellebecq is back under investigation by a judge, this time for comments made in 2022 in an interview with the outlet Front Populaire. The investigation was instigated by a complaint from the Grand Mosque of Paris in 2023 and may result in criminal charges.Here’s some of what he said. (Translation by The Critic. It sounds better in French):The wish of the native French population is not that Muslims assimilate but that they stop robbing and assaulting them. Or, another solution, that they leave. … When entire territories come under Islamist control, I think acts of resistance will take place. There will be attacks and shootings in mosques, in cafés frequented by Muslims, in short, Bataclans in reverse.The “great replacement” theory “[is] not a theory, it’s a fact. It’s statistical evidence.”The first two statements are his opinion. The second is unsavory, especially given the reportedly racially motivated October murder in Paris of a black French national. But it is his prediction, not an incitement to violence.The third statement, as Houellebecq says, is fact. European populations across the West are shrinking, while foreign peoples immigrate in large numbers. One thus replaces the other. We can discuss whether this is good or bad, or why it happens, but not the undeniable fact that it is occurring.But whether he is right or wrong is not the issue. The protesters taking to the streets every week in France are motivated by various causes from teacher shortages to pensions to Gaza, not an interview in Front Populaire they never read. I doubt any of the young men in Marseille looting luxury stores for sneakers and bags have read a book, let alone one by Michel Houellebecq.>>> The Unexpected Source of Muslim Immigration to FranceIn a recent interview with Ben Shapiro, comedian and writer Rob Schneider said:When the truth becomes a right-wing concept, then I think you have to stand up for it…It’s going to cost you to speak your opinion. It’s going to cost you jobs, it’s going to cost you money, but it’s going to cost you more if you don’t speak up and you lose this incredible experiment in freedom that we have.America was founded on free speech, which is the only way to get to the truth. If we lose that, we lose all. France’s revolution followed ours by 13 years. But whereas ours was against an occupying overseas power, theirs was internal and devolved into a purge for ideological purity. Free speech was the very basis of our revolution, but it was an early casualty in theirs.I was U.S. Consul in Slovakia for three years. Everyone my age there remembered life under communism. The system survived partly because of the Soviet Union’s threat of military force, which they used in Hungary in 1956 and Czechoslovakia in 1968 to suppress popular uprisings. But Czechoslovakia and the other Soviet satellite states also had repressive police, informers, and political prisons to keep people down.People shared bitter jokes, such as “we pretend to work, and they pretend to pay us,” about socialist economics.
